name: Zig
typeSystem: Static, strong, inferred. Comptime (compile-time evaluation) replaces generics and macros: type parameters are ordinary values computed at compile time, giving duck-typed generics without a separate syntax.

typeSystemExample.caption: Generic max via comptime type parameter

runtime: Compiled ahead-of-time to native code via LLVM (or its own x86-64 backend). No hidden control flow, no garbage collector; optional safety checks can be disabled in release builds.

runtimes.name: Native (LLVM backend)
runtimes.role: Default production backend using LLVM for optimised machine code across many targets.

runtimes.name: Native (self-hosted x86_64 backend)
runtimes.role: Incremental backend written in Zig, aimed at much faster debug-build compile times.

runtimes.name: WebAssembly (wasm32-freestanding / wasm32-wasi)
runtimes.role: First-class WASM targets for browsers and WASI runtimes.

compilers.name: zig (self-hosted)
compilers.role: The official compiler, itself written in Zig; uses LLVM or its own codegen backend.

compilers.name: zig cc
compilers.role: Drop-in C/C++ cross-compiler wrapping Clang/LLVM, bundled with the Zig toolchain.

concurrencyModel: Async/await with stackless coroutines existed in earlier versions but was removed in 0.11. Current Zig relies on OS threads (std.Thread) plus an event-based I/O model (std.io.poll). No hidden allocations or runtime scheduler.

concurrencyExample.caption: 4 threads computing i*i in parallel via std.Thread
